theory.overview: Quantum protocols leverage entanglement and superposition for tasks impossible classically. Quantum teleportation transmits quantum states using classical communication and shared entanglement. Superdense coding sends two classical bits per qubit. These demonstrate quantum information fundamentals and enable quantum networks.

sections.title: Quantum Teleportation
sections.content: Teleportation transmits an arbitrary quantum state using 1 ebit (Bell pair) and 2 classical bits. Alice has unknown state |ψ⟩ and shares |Φ⁺⟩ with Bob. Alice Bell-measures her qubits, sends 2 classical bits to Bob, who applies corrections to recover |ψ⟩. Does not clone (original destroyed) and respects no-communication theorem (Bob needs classical bits).

sections.title: Superdense Coding
sections.content: Sends 2 classical bits using 1 qubit and shared entanglement. Alice encodes 2 bits by applying I, X, Z, or XZ to her half of |Φ⁺⟩, sends to Bob who Bell-measures to recover the bits. Doubles classical capacity of quantum channel with entanglement assistance.

sections.title: Quantum Key Distribution
sections.content: BB84 protocol: Alice sends qubits in random bases, Bob measures in random bases, they compare bases publicly and keep matching bits. Eavesdropping introduces detectable errors (25% for intercept-resend). Information-theoretic security from no-cloning and measurement disturbance.

practiceProblems.description: What resources does quantum teleportation require?
practiceProblems.explanation: Teleportation requires 1 ebit (shared entanglement) and 2 classical bits to transmit 1 qubit.
